stories.head: IBM survey finds a gap between AI responsibility and investment authority
stories.fact: IBM reports that only 18% of surveyed chief AI officers fully control AI investment decisions, while 29% say their organizations quickly redirect decisions and resources when performance insights identify improvements.
stories.why: Assign explicit authority to pause, resize or retire AI workflows; measure business outcomes rather than model adoption alone.
stories.unc: Survey responses are self-reported associations, not causal proof that a particular governance structure improves returns.
stories.credit: IBM Institute for Business Value, November 17, 2026
stories.alt: Survey panel contrasts 18% full investment control with 29% rapid response to performance insights and labels the causal limitation.

stories.head: Credit-risk research separates price calibration from hedge-transfer risk
stories.date: arXiv new listing November 17; submission record October 30, 2026
stories.fact: Di Persio and Mattesini use adapted Wasserstein distance to compare how credit models reveal information over time. Models matching current bond prices can still imply different rating dynamics and hedging errors.
stories.why: Add model-transfer stress tests to calibration checks; compare hedges under alternative information dynamics rather than accepting a single fitted model.
stories.unc: Theoretical and numerical research is not a demonstrated trading edge. The November 17 listing and October 30 submission dates differ; this is not represented as a paper first written today.
stories.alt: Conceptual diagram distinguishes matching current bond prices from differing future information paths and hedge-transfer risk.

stories.head: Monday selloff leaves technology and broad-market risk exposed
stories.date: November 16 regular-session close; AP report retrieved November 17, 2026
stories.fact: The S&P 500 closed Monday at 7,416.59, down 1.9%, its third consecutive loss. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.5% and the Dow fell 1.4%, according to AP.
stories.why: Reassess correlated downside exposure and opening-auction participation; a prior-close loss does not establish current executable liquidity.
stories.unc: These are November 16 index closes, not November 17 futures, SPY or QQQ quotes. No current order-book depth was verified.
stories.alt: Prior-close panel labels November 16 S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite and Dow declines; it contains no live futures claim.

stories.head: Warsh frames advanced AI as a productivity and policy scenario problem
stories.fact: At the Fed's Productivity and Jobs Task Force Conference, Kevin Warsh emphasized uncertainty about the magnitude and timing of advanced AI's economic effects. Board staff have begun evaluating contingencies with stylized model-based scenarios.
stories.why: Stress alternative productivity and adoption paths in macro-sensitive models; avoid hard-coding a single AI-driven growth or rate outcome.
stories.unc: The remarks supply no precise productivity forecast and announce no new FOMC rate decision.
stories.alt: Policy scenario panel identifies uncertainty in AI productivity timing, contingency analysis and the absence of a rate decision.

stories.head: Home Depot reports sales growth and updates its annual outlook
stories.fact: Home Depot reported third-quarter sales of $43.4 billion, up 4.9%, with comparable sales up 2.2%. Diluted EPS was $3.72 and adjusted diluted EPS $3.86. Its updated full-year sales-growth guidance is approximately 4.5%.
stories.why: Separate comparable demand, acquisition effects and adjusted earnings when evaluating consumer and housing exposure.
stories.unc: Guidance is forward-looking. Adjusted EPS differs from GAAP EPS; reported sales growth alone does not establish broad household demand strength.
stories.credit: Home Depot fiscal Q3 release, November 17, 2026
stories.alt: Results panel separates total and comparable sales growth, GAAP and adjusted EPS, and forward-looking annual guidance.
